Argument Mapper Help

Build an argument

Start with your main contention: the claim you are arguing for. Select a box, then add a support, an objection or a weak objection under it. Co-premises sit side by side and work together as one reason; separate groups under a box are separate arguments.

Double-click a box to edit it (with Edit: Single, one click). Right-click a box or the canvas for more options; on a touch screen, press and hold.

Main argument: white (dark gray in the light theme)
Objection: red
Rebuttal of an objection: orange
Weak objection or rebuttal: dashed

A support takes the color of the argument it belongs to. A weak objection says a claim hasn't been shown, without saying it's false. Notes are comments, not premises.

Check the logic

Turn on Deductive to check each step. Every step gets a tag:

  • ✓ and a rule name: the conclusion follows from its premises. (It doesn't say the premises are true.)
  • ? not recognized: the checker can't confirm the step.
  • ? with a reason, such as ? ambiguous: a box can be read more than one way. Click the tag to choose what you mean, and your choice is written into the box.
  • ✗ with a reason: something to fix first, such as because inside a box (a box holds one claim; put the reason in a box below it). Click the tag to see what.

The colors button after Deductive (Shift+C) colors each premise by its part in the step: where premises meet, a color; words that deny what another premise says, red; a part the conclusion denies, underlined in red dashes. Once a step is valid, what goes on to the conclusion is one stretch: plain in colors 1, which dims the rest; green and underlined in colors 2, which dims nothing. Until then each part has its own color. Each press moves on: off, 1, 2, off.

Commas can settle what you mean: Mary sang, and danced, in the hall (both in the hall); Mary sang, and she danced in the hall (only the dancing). So can both … and, either … or, implies (If A implies B, then C) and brackets. Symbols work too: ~ & ∨ → ↔ ∀ ∃.

✓ Warranted means the main contention is established by the argument as it stands; ✗ Unwarranted means it isn't yet, not that it's false. The Logic panel lists the rules the checker uses.

Reuse premises

To use a premise again in another argument, choose Add Cross-Reference from a box's menu, then click the original; Reference Arguments (or the box's ↗ badge) groups such premises into arguments for or against the box, each checked as a step. To name another premise in a box's text (If S7 and S8, then S4), choose Link a premise from the right-click menu while editing.

Arrange and annotate

Drop a box beside another to make it a co-premise, below a box to make it a child, or above one to make it a parent. Hold Shift as you drop to leave it unconnected. To move a box without its children, hold its ⠿ handle until it turns into ✥, then drag. Place: Free keeps boxes where you drop them.

Implicit marks an unstated assumption, and Given a premise accepted without argument. Evaluate marks a box and adds comments; Evaluations lists them. Review locks the map except for evaluations.

On a touch screen

Press and hold a box or the canvas for its menu, or a button to see what it does. On an iPhone or iPad, Save to File opens the share sheet: choose Save to Files.

Save and share

Save to File saves the map. Save As saves a copy as the map, a picture (PNG, JPEG, SVG), a PDF or a text outline. Recent Maps keeps copies in this browser, and the save indicator shows where the map is saved. String Mode edits the map as text; Collaborate shares it for live editing.

Keyboard shortcuts and formatting

Shortcuts act on the selected box when you aren't typing.

Add a support / objection / weak objectionEnter / Shift+Enter / Ctrl+Enter
Add a co-premise on the right / leftTab / Shift+Tab
Add a parent / noteAlt+↑ / Alt+Enter
Make it a support / objection; switch weak and strongS / O; W
Implicit / main / given / noteI / U / G / N
Undo / redoCtrl+Z / Ctrl+Y
Save / save asCtrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S
Search the map (after clicking it)Ctrl+F
Fit the map / center itZ / C
Deductive check / check one stepK / Shift+K
Edit with one click / place freelyShift+E / Shift+F
Help / stop editing/ / Esc

Formatting (turn on Rich text first): type **bold**, *italic*, [text](url) or $…$ for math and it converts as you type, or select words and press Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I or Ctrl+U. With boxes selected instead, these (or B, I, U in a box's menu or under Formatting) format whole boxes. Backspace selects a premise link or a formula, then deletes it; double-click a formula to edit it.

Deductive check

Each row is a step: a group of premises and the box they support. ✓ means the conclusion follows by a rule the checker knows; an unmarked step may still be a good argument. Click a row to go to it.
